title: Leadership and behavioral questions -- STAR preparation
exp: Lead I questions test whether you can influence, mentor, and commit -- not just execute. Prepare 5 STAR stories from your real work.
pts: STAR: Situation (context) -> Task (your responsibility) -> Action (what YOU did) -> Result (measurable outcome). Under 2 minutes.
5 stories: technical disagreement, mentoring a colleague, production incident owned, pushed back on a deadline, decision you'd change today.
Disagreement stories: did you raise it with data/reasoning? Did you support the outcome afterward?
Your material: BMS migration, ComplySec360 evidence pipeline, SCIM provisioning, Zintara AI platform.

viz.note: STAR: S(1-2 sentences) -> T(your responsibility) -> A(what YOU did) -> R(measurable result). Under 2 minutes total. Practice until you don't need notes.

qa.q: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision.
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Template: describe the decision and why you disagreed. How you raised it -- specific reasoning or a small prototype, not just opinion. Result: even if overruled, you supported the team decision and ideally something from your concern was addressed. Interviewers want professional disagreement AND commitment afterward.

qa.q: How would you push back on an unrealistic deadline?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Lead with trade-offs not refusal: we can hit that date if we scope to X, or hit full scope two weeks later. Give the decision-maker a real choice. Back it with a breakdown of remaining work. Accept they might still choose the original deadline -- your job is ensuring they decide with full information.

qa.q: What does code review mean to you?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Beyond syntax: correctness under edge cases, testability, security/performance risks (non-parameterized query, .collect() on a large DataFrame), intent clarity for someone reading cold in 6 months. Also: specific positive feedback so people understand what good looks like, not just what's wrong.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** T-SQL engine parses, compiles into execution plans, caches them in the plan cache, and executes via the storage engine (buffer pool & latching).

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Parameter sniffing and missing stats cause sub-optimal plan compilation, resulting in full table scans and high CPU.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Parameterization improves plan reuse, but recompile hints (OPTION RECOMPILE) may be needed for skewed data distributions.
